question_text: What helped in the colonisation of Asian and African countries? Identify the correct statement from the following options.
options: Intergovernmental policies for the expansion of trade
Governmental invite to the mother countries for expansion
Technology, investments and improvement in transport
Capitalists of these regions wanted trade with colonial powers
answer_text: Technology, investments and improvement in transport
answer_explanation: Modern technology, capital investment and better transport enabled European powers to penetrate, control and economically exploit Asian and African regions.

question_text: Arrange the following in chronological order: I. Print culture created the conditions for the French Revolution II. Martin Luther’s writings led to beginning of the Protestant Reformation III. Menocchio reinterpreted the message of the Bible IV. Johann Gutenberg invented Printing press OPTIONS:

question_text: Identify the crop with the help of the following information - It is a crop which is used both as food and fodder. - It is a kharif crop which requires temperature between 21°C to 27°C. - It grows well in old alluvial soil. - Use of modern inputs have contributed to the increasing production of this crop. Options:
answer_text: Maize
answer_explanation: Maize is a kharif crop used as both food and fodder; it grows well at 21°C–27°C, especially in old alluvial soil.

question_text: Which of the following description of forest is NOT correct?
options: Reserved Forest -Reservation of more than half of forests
Protected Forest- Reservation of 1/3 of the forests
Unclassed Forest-Reservation of forest under govt. and private individuals
Permanent Forest-Reserved and unclassed forest for the production of timber
answer_text: Permanent Forest-Reserved and unclassed forest for the production of timber
answer_explanation: Permanent forests consist mainly of reserved and protected forests, not reserved and unclassed forests.

question_text: Match the following: RESOURCES - EXAMPLES. a. Renewable Resources - I. Forests and wildlife; b. Non-Renewable Resources - II. The oceanic resources; c. National Resources - III. Roads, canals and railway; d. International Resources - IV. Minerals and fossil fuels.
answer_text: a-I, b-IV, c-III, d-II
answer_explanation: Forests and wildlife are renewable, minerals and fossil fuels are non-renewable, roads/canals/railways are national resources, and oceanic resources beyond national jurisdiction are international resources.

Community government elected by people belonging to one language community

question_text: Analyse any two factors that were responsible for the Great Depression in America during 1929. 2
answer_text:
Any two factors:
1. Agricultural overproduction caused a sharp fall in prices, reducing farmers’ incomes and their ability to repay loans.
2. In October 1929, the Wall Street stock market crashed; banks failed, credit contracted, factories closed and unemployment rose.
3. The withdrawal of US loans from overseas markets deepened the crisis internationally. (Any two)
answer_explanation: Overproduction weakened purchasing power, while the financial crash and banking failures sharply reduced investment, production and employment.

question_text: Mention the provisions that constitute India into a secular country. 2
answer_text:
Any two provisions:
1. The Constitution does not establish any official religion for the Indian state.
2. All citizens have freedom to profess, practise and propagate any religion, or not follow any religion.
3. The state cannot discriminate among citizens on grounds of religion.
4. The state may intervene in religious matters to ensure equality and reform. (Any two)
answer_explanation: These provisions keep the state neutral toward religions while protecting equal religious freedom for all citizens.

question_text: Suggest any two ways to conserve energy resources in India. OR Suggest any two ways to improve the usage of Solar energy.
answer_text:
Energy conservation — any two:
1. Use public transport, car-pooling and fuel-efficient vehicles, and switch off appliances when not needed.
2. Promote renewable energy, energy-efficient equipment and careful use of electricity and fossil fuels.

OR

Improving solar-energy use — any two:
1. Install solar panels, solar water heaters, cookers and street lights in homes, institutions and public places.
2. Provide subsidies, affordable credit, research support and grid connectivity for solar projects.
answer_explanation: Conservation lowers waste and demand for exhaustible fuels, while wider adoption and policy support make solar energy more accessible and economical.

question_text: In what ways Government can increase employment in the rural sector? 2 SECTION C SHORT ANSWER BASED QUESTIONS (3X5=15)
answer_text:
Any two measures:
1. Invest in irrigation, roads, storage, transport, schools and health centres to create construction and service jobs.
2. Promote small-scale industries, food processing, dairy, poultry, fisheries and other allied activities.
3. Implement rural employment programmes such as MGNREGA effectively. (Any two)
answer_explanation: Public investment and diversification beyond farming create both wage employment and self-employment in rural areas.

question_text: How was the social and political situation of India affected by the First World War? Explain. OR How did the Indian merchants and industrialist s relate themselves to the Civil Disobedience Movement? Explain.
answer_text:
First World War effects on India — any three:
1. Defence expenditure increased sharply and was financed through war loans and higher taxes.
2. Customs duties were raised and income tax was introduced.
3. Prices doubled between 1913 and 1918, causing severe hardship.
4. Villages faced forced recruitment, crop failures and the influenza epidemic, leading to widespread suffering. (Any three)

OR

Merchants and industrialists in the Civil Disobedience Movement — any three:
1. They wanted protection against imports and a favourable rupee–sterling exchange ratio.
2. They formed organisations such as FICCI and supported the movement financially.
3. They refused to buy or sell imported goods and backed the boycott.
4. Their support later weakened because of concern over prolonged disruption and the growing influence of workers. (Any three)
answer_explanation: The war imposed heavy economic and social burdens on Indians. Business groups initially supported civil disobedience because nationalist demands aligned with their commercial interests.

question_text: Examine the factors that influence the distribution pattern of the railway network in India. 3
answer_text:
The railway network is influenced by:
1. Relief and terrain: flat northern plains favour dense tracks, while mountains, deserts, marshes and forested areas make construction difficult.
2. Population and economic activity: densely populated, agricultural, industrial and mining regions have greater demand for rail transport.
3. Administrative and strategic needs, availability of capital, and links to ports and major cities also shape routes.
answer_explanation: Railways develop most where construction is physically easier and passenger/freight demand is high; difficult terrain and sparse settlement reduce network density.

question_text: In what ways Multi National Corporation (MNC) different from other companies? Explain with an example.
answer_text:
1. An MNC owns or controls production in more than one country, whereas an ordinary company may operate mainly within one country.
2. It has large financial and technological resources and coordinates production globally.
3. It may set up factories, acquire local companies, form partnerships or place orders with small producers.
Example: An automobile MNC may manufacture components in India, assemble vehicles in another country and sell them worldwide.
answer_explanation: MNCs organise investment, production and markets across national borders, linking local producers to global production networks.

question_text: Differentiate between democratic and non-democratic government. 3
answer_text:
Democratic government:
1. Rulers are elected through regular, free and fair elections.
2. Decisions follow constitutional rules and citizens enjoy rights and accountability.
3. Opposition, public debate and peaceful change of rulers are permitted.

Non-democratic government:
1. Rulers are not genuinely elected or elections are not free and fair.
2. Power is concentrated and decisions may ignore constitutional limits and public opinion.
3. Rights, opposition and political competition are restricted.
answer_explanation: The basic distinction is popular consent and accountability: democracies derive authority from citizens, while non-democratic regimes concentrate power without effective public control.

question_text: ‘Tertiary sector is different from other sectors.’ Justify the statement with suitable arguments. 3 SECTION D LONG ANSWER BASED QUESTIONS (5X4=20)
answer_text:
1. The tertiary sector does not directly produce goods; it provides services that support production and consumption.
2. It includes transport, storage, communication, banking, trade, education, health and administration.
3. Its growth is driven by the development of agriculture and industry, rising incomes and the need for essential and specialised services.
answer_explanation: Primary and secondary sectors produce natural or manufactured goods, whereas the tertiary sector facilitates these activities and supplies services to people and enterprises.

question_text: Highlight the various measures and practices that French revolutionaries introduced to create a sense of collective identity amongst the French people. OR Highlight the role of Otto Von Bismarck in making of Germany.
answer_text:
French revolutionaries created collective identity through the following measures:
1. They introduced the ideas of la patrie (the fatherland) and le citoyen (the citizen), stressing equal rights under a constitution.
2. The royal standard was replaced by the tricolour flag.
3. The Estates-General was elected by active citizens and renamed the National Assembly.
4. New hymns, oaths and martyrs were commemorated in the name of the nation.
5. A centralised administrative system and uniform laws, weights and measures were introduced; internal customs duties were abolished and French was promoted as a common language.

OR

Role of Otto von Bismarck in German unification:
1. As Prussia’s chief minister, Bismarck led unification through a policy of ‘blood and iron’.
2. He used the Prussian army and bureaucracy to defeat opposition.
3. Three wars over seven years—with Denmark, Austria and France—ended in Prussian victory.
4. The German states were united under Prussian leadership.
5. In January 1871, the German Empire was proclaimed at Versailles and William I became German Emperor.
answer_explanation: The French revolutionaries used shared symbols, institutions and uniform administration to transform subjects into citizens. Bismarck achieved German unity through Prussian military power and diplomacy.

question_text: ‘Manufacturing sector is considered as the backbone of general and economic development.’ Examine the statement in the context of India. OR Examine the multi-pronged aspects of Information Technology and Electronics Industry.
answer_text:
Manufacturing is the backbone of development because:
1. It modernises agriculture by supplying machinery, fertilisers and equipment.
2. It reduces dependence on agriculture by creating jobs in secondary and tertiary activities.
3. It adds value to raw materials and increases national income.
4. It supports exports, earns foreign exchange and improves the trade balance.
5. Industrial growth helps reduce poverty and regional disparities and promotes overall economic development.

OR

Information Technology and Electronics Industry:
1. It produces products ranging from radios, televisions and telephones to computers, telecom equipment and advanced electronic systems.
2. It supports communication, banking, education, governance, defence and industrial automation.
3. It generates substantial employment, especially for skilled workers and women.
4. Software technology parks and major centres such as Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai, Noida and Mumbai promote exports.
5. It has earned foreign exchange and made India an important global IT and business-services hub.
answer_explanation: Manufacturing links agriculture, industry and services while generating jobs and exports. The IT-electronics sector has a wide product base and strong multiplier effects across the economy.

question_text: Describe the role of political parties in India. OR Describe the necessity or utility of political parties in democratic countries.
answer_text:
Roles/necessity of political parties:
1. They contest elections and offer different policies and programmes.
2. The winning party or coalition forms and runs the government.
3. Parties make laws through their elected representatives.
4. Opposition parties scrutinise the government, criticise failures and offer alternatives.
5. Parties shape public opinion, raise issues and provide people access to government machinery and welfare schemes.
6. They recruit leaders and coordinate diverse social interests into workable policies. (Any five)
answer_explanation: Modern democracies need political parties to organise electoral competition, form governments, represent interests and hold rulers accountable.

question_text: Explain the role of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) in the rural society. OR Explain the significance of The Reserve Bank of India in the Indian economy. SECTION-E CASE BASED QUESTIONS (4x3=12)
answer_text:
Role of Self-Help Groups in rural society:
1. SHGs organise poor people, especially women, into small groups that save regularly.
2. Members obtain small loans from the pooled savings without demanding heavy collateral.
3. Banks lend to the group, improving access to formal credit and reducing dependence on moneylenders.
4. Loans support self-employment, emergencies and household needs at reasonable interest.
5. Group meetings build financial discipline, collective decision-making and women’s social and economic empowerment.

OR

Significance of the Reserve Bank of India:
1. RBI issues currency and acts as the central bank of India.
2. It supervises banks and ensures that they maintain required cash reserves.
3. It regulates the supply of money and credit through monetary policy.
4. It monitors formal lenders so that banks lend to productive sectors and weaker sections.
5. It acts as banker to the government and helps maintain financial stability.
answer_explanation: SHGs expand affordable credit and collective empowerment at the grassroots. RBI regulates the banking system and credit conditions to support stability and balanced development.

question_text: Read the source given below and answer the question that follows: Will Thorne is one of those who went in search of seasonal work, loading bricks and doing odd jobs. He describes how job-seekers walked to London in search of work: ‘I had always wanted to go to London, and my desire ... was stimulated by letters from an old workmate ... who was now working at the Old Kent Road Gas Works ... I finally decided to go ... in November, 1881. With two friends I started out to walk the journey, filled with the hope that we would be able to obtain employment, when we get there, with the kind assistance of my friend ... we had little money when we started, not enough to pay for our food and lodgings each night until we arrived in London. Some days we walked as much as twenty miles, and other days less. Our money was gone at the end of the third day ... For two nights we slept out – once under a haystack, and once in an old farm shed ... On arrival in London we tried to find ... my friend ... but ... were unsuccessful. Our money was gone, so there was nothing for us to do but to walk around until late at night, and then try to find some place to sleep. We found an old building and slept in it that night. The next day, Sunday, late in the afternoon, we got to the Old Kent Gas Works, and applied for work. To my great surprise, the man we had been looking for was working at the time. He spoke to the foreman and I was given a job.’ Quoted in Raphael Samuel, ‘Comers and Goers’, in H.J. Dyos and Michael Wolff, eds, The Victorian City: Images and Realities, 1973. 34.1 Analyse the major factor which led London become an attractive place for the job seekers. 34.2 Analyse the reason for the appointment of Will Thorne by the Old Kent Gas works. 34.3 Examine the preference of hand labour over machi nes by the industrialists of the Victorian Britain.
answer_text:
34.1 London attracted job-seekers because it was a major industrial and commercial city offering seasonal work, factories, docks, construction and varied urban employment.
34.2 Will Thorne obtained work through his old workmate, who recommended him to the foreman at the Old Kent Road Gas Works.
34.3 Victorian industrialists preferred hand labour because labour was abundant and cheap, machines required costly investment, demand often fluctuated seasonally, and many products needed variety, delicate workmanship or human skill that machines could not easily provide.
answer_explanation: The extract highlights urban employment opportunities and the importance of personal contacts. In Victorian Britain, low wages and flexible skilled labour often made manual production more economical than machinery.

question_text: Read the given extract and answer following questions Narmada Bachao Andolan or Save Narmada Movement is a Non -Governmental Organisation (NGO) that mobilized tribal people, farmers, environmentalists and human rights activists against the Sardar Sarovar Dam being built across the Narmada river in Gujarat. It originally focused on the environmental issues related to trees that would be submerged under the dam water. Recently it has re-focused the aim to enable poor citizens, especially the oustees (displaced people) to get full rehabilitation facilities from the government. People felt that their suffering would not be in vain... accepted the trauma of displaceme nt believing in the promise of irrigated fields and plentiful harvests. So, often the survivors of Rihand told us that they accepted their sufferings as sacrifice for the sake of their nation. But now, after thirty bitter years of being adrift, their livel ihood having even being more precarious, they keep asking: “Are we the only ones chosen to make sacrifices for the nation?” Source: S. Sharma, quoted in In the Belly of the River. Tribal conflicts over development in Narmada valley. A. Baviskar. 1995. 35.1 With what objective ‘Sardar Sarovar Dam’ was built? 35.2 Analyse the reason of protest by the tribal people. 35.3 Highlight the issues on which ‘Save Narmada Movement’ worked on.
answer_text:
35.1 The Sardar Sarovar Dam was built to provide irrigation, hydroelectric power and water supply, thereby supporting agricultural and regional development.
35.2 Tribal people protested because the dam submerged forests and villages, displaced them from land and livelihoods, and rehabilitation and compensation were inadequate or delayed.
35.3 The Save Narmada Movement worked on environmental damage, protection of forests and river ecology, rights of displaced people, fair compensation, and complete rehabilitation of oustees.
answer_explanation: Large dams promise development benefits but can impose severe environmental and social costs. The movement therefore linked ecological protection with justice for displaced communities.

question_text: Read the given extract and answer following questions. Power sharing arrangements can also be seen in the way political parties, pressure groups and movements control or influence those in power. In a democracy, the citizens must have freedom to choose among various contenders for power. In contemporary democracies, this takes the form of competition among different parties. Such competition ensures that power does not remain in one hand. In the long run, power is shared among different political parties that represent different ideologies and social groups. So metimes this kind of sharing can be direct, when two or more parties form an alliance to contest elections. If their alliance is elected, they form a coalition government and thus share power. In a democracy, we find interest groups such as those of traders, businessmen, industrialists, farmers and industrial workers. They also will have share in governmental power, either through participation in governmental committees or bringing influence on the decision-making process. 36.1 ‘Power sharing is an essen tial component of democracy.’ Give one example to prove the statement. 36.2 How is alliance building an example of power sharing? 36.3 How Political parties, pressure groups and movements help in controlling or influencing those who are in power? SECTION-F MAP SKILL BASED QUESTION (2+3=5) 37 37a. Two places A and B have been marked on the given outline map of India. 2 Identify them and write their correct names on the lines drawn near them. A. Indian National Congress session at this place in 1920 B. The place where Mahatma Gandhi broke Salt Law. 37b. On the same outline map of India locate and label any THREE of the following with suitable Symbols. a. Hirakud Dam b. Tarapur Atomic Power Station c. Noida Software Technology Park d. Kochi Port Note: The following questions are for Visually Impaired Candidates only in lieu of Q. No.37. Attempt any FIVE questions.
answer_text:
36.1 Example: In a coalition government, two or more political parties jointly exercise power, preventing its concentration in one party.
36.2 Parties form an alliance to contest elections; if elected, they form a coalition government and share ministerial positions and decision-making.
36.3 Political parties compete in elections and act as opposition, while pressure groups and movements influence policies through campaigns, public mobilisation, representation on committees and pressure on decision-makers.
answer_explanation: Democratic power sharing operates through electoral competition, coalitions and organised social influence, ensuring that multiple groups participate in governance.
